subject: MAP: Inference stress testing plan & success criteria
messages:
From: Priya Natarajan <priya@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@nebulasys.com>
Cc: Samantha Kline <samantha@nebulasys.com>
Date: 2027-04-11T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: MAP: Inference stress testing plan & success criteria

Hi Jordan / Samantha —

Thanks for the call this morning. Per our MAP, attached is a first draft of the performance validation checklist and the workload matrix (nebula_map_draft.xlsx). I sketched the scope we discussed so we can lock the test window and acceptance gates: 

- Scope: baseline + peak traffic simulation for chat endpoint (user prompt -> first token latency + sustained throughput for 10m windows)
- Workload slices: 80% short prompts (<=64 tokens), 15% medium (65-256), 5% long (>256)
- Concurrency targets: ramp to 150 concurrent streams, steady at 100 for the peak phase
- Key SLOs / success criteria:
  - TTFT (Time-to-first-token) p95 <= 180ms at steady peak
  - Token throughput >= 8k tokens/s sustained across 10m window
  - Error rate <= 0.5% (5xx / client errors)
  - KV/prefix cache hit rate >= 60% during steady state (if enabled)
- Test plan: warmup (30m), three 10m steady-state legs, cool-down. Include a canary run day-before for safety.

Action items I need from you to finalize schedule:
1) Confirm peak QPS expectation and whether you want us to run with or without prefix caching.
2) Confirm the model variant you will pin for the pilot (v2.1-quant vs v2.1-fp16).
3) Approve test window: Thurs 2027-04-15 02:00–06:00 UTC (suggested) or propose alternate.

I've CC'd Priyom (infrastructure) and Marissa (CS) so they can scope the harness and acceptance signal collection. Attaching a lightweight stress-config.yml that outlines the scenarios.

Thanks — look forward to locking this in.

— Priya Natarajan
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
priya@redwood.com
redwood.com

Attachments: nebula_map_draft.xlsx (workload matrix), stress-config.yml (scenario stubs)

Priya — thanks, this looks like the right level of detail. A couple quick clarifications from our side: 

- Peak QPS: we need to validate 1,200 requests/minute sustained (that maps to your 100 concurrent streams in our estimate).
- Model: we'll pin v2.1-quant for the pilot but want a post-run compare against v2.1-fp16 for quality/loss checks.
- Cache: please run both variants (cache ON / cache OFF) as separate legs — we'd like to understand sensitivity.
- Canary: agreed on a short canary 24h prior. 

One ask: can you include TTFT p50/p90/p95 and also per-request token-generation rate (tokens/s) so we can map to billing/extract unit costs?

If Thu 15 Apr is your preferred slot, that works for us. Scheduling note: our infra team (Samantha) will provide temporary API keys; I'll share them once we lock the time.

Thanks — Jordan

Thanks Priya — looping in a quick technical draft for the harness and observable signals. Highlights: 

- Test harness: Redwood's perf-harness (k6 driver -> long-lived HTTP streams to mimic streaming chat). We'll run two orthogonal legs: (A) cache OFF, (B) cache ON. Each leg: warmup 30m, 3x steady minutes of 10m, cool-down.
- Concurrency handling: use connection pools with 150 parallel client sessions; ramp schedule: 0 -> 50 -> 100 -> 150 over 20m. Validate autoscale behavior for Dedicated capacity fallback.
- Metrics to capture (per-token and per-request): TTFT p50/p90/p95, token_throughput (tokens/s), gen_token_latency distribution, request_time_total, 5xx_count, client_error_count, cache_hit_rate. We will emit traces and full token timestamps to the test bucket.
- Failure handling: if TTFT p95 > 350ms for more than one 10m leg we mark the leg FAILED. If error rate > 1% or sustained token throughput is < 75% of target across two legs, escalate.
- Artifacts: stress-config.yml (attached), runbook.md (drive link), and Grafana dashboard link for live view.

I'll provision a dedicated test API key and a write-only test bucket for logs. Priya — want me to simulate the v2.1-fp16 run as a separate post-check? That will extend the window by ~90m.

— Priyom
Senior Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference
priyom_das@redwood.com
